I could find *no credible evidence* that matches the described event (anthropologists in Vietnam using AI to solve a long-standing problem over 160 years old) as of **November 21, 2026**. Here's what I found:

---

## What I Searched

- Vietnamese media (Vietnam.vn and others) for a story titled *“Para ahli antropologi berhasil menggunakan AI untuk memecahkan masalah yang telah ada selama lebih dari 160 tahun.”*
- Scientific databases, news outlets, and academic publications for “anthropology”, “AI”, “Vietnam”, and “160 years / over 160 years / longstanding” together.
- Records of high-profile cases where AI in anthropology solved a centuries-old or ~160-year-old problem.

---

## What I Found

### Mathematicians, Not Anthropologists

- There *is* a Malaysian/ Vietnamese case of **Vietnamese mathematicians** Vu Khac Ky and Tuan Tran solving the *Courtade–Kumar conjecture* (an information theory problem from 2013) by using AI to help test ideas and counterexamples. ([e.vnexpress.net](https://e.vnexpress.net/news/tech/personalities/vietnamese-mathematicians-solve-decade-old-information-theory-problem-5125621.html?utm_source=openai))  
- The math problem was around 13 years old, not 160+. So **not fitting** the description. ([e.vnexpress.net](https://e.vnexpress.net/news/tech/personalities/vietnamese-mathematicians-solve-decade-old-information-theory-problem-5125621.html?utm_source=openai))

### Anthropology & AI in Vietnam

- There is reporting on **AI applications in social sciences and humanities in Vietnam**: using AI in anthropology, linguistics, cultural studies to process unstructured data (texts, interviews, media), analyze rituals etc. But these are general applications, tools, workshops, strategy discussions—not a specific solved problem that had stood unsolved for ~160 years. ([en.nhandan.vn](https://en.nhandan.vn/ai-applications-in-social-sciences-and-humanities-post150731.html?utm_source=openai))  
- One Vietnamese journal article (“Engaging with Postmodernist Anthropology: Potential and Prospects for Digital Anthropology in Vietnam”) discusses digital and postmodernist anthropology, but is theoretical; no solved longstanding problem claimed. ([jossh.ussh.edu.vn](https://jossh.ussh.edu.vn/index.php/JOSSH-VN/article/view/742?utm_source=openai))  

### Global Anthropology & AI Claims

- There are several scholarly works arguing for deeper integration of AI and computational methods in anthropology: e.g. “Closing the loop: Relocated expertise …” which describes using AI (LLMs) to help build bibliographic data, missing records, etc. But again, no reference to a specific problem unresolved for 160 years that has *just now been solved*. ([tandfonline.com](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00187259.2026.2717593?needAccess=true&scroll=top&utm_source=openai))  
- Another article “Digital Anthropology Meets Data Science” outlines methodological changes and case studies, but again, all are relatively recent, data-driven projects. ([anthropology-news.org](https://www.anthropology-news.org/articles/digital-anthropology-meets-data-science/?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Assessment

Based on available sources:

- **No evidence** of any anthropological discovery in Vietnam where AI solved a problem that had been unsolved for ~160 years.  
- The story likely originates from a *misinterpretation*, *misreporting*, or a *press release/claim* that hasn’t been substantiated with primary evidence.

---

## Conclusion

I cannot confirm that the candidate headline/event (“Anthropologists use AI to solve long-standing problems of over 160 years in Vietnam”) is accurate. If you like, I can attempt to track outreach or calls to Vietnamese universities or scientific journals to see if there *is* an unpublished result, but as of now, it appears to be *unverified* or misattributed.  

Would you prefer me to try to dig more deeply (e.g. Vietnamese-language sources or contacts)?

Here is a factual research note on the event “Espírito Santo preserves and recovers 25,000 hectares of forests”:

---

## What Happened

1. **Achievement Completed**  
   The government of the state of Espírito Santo, Brazil, reports that *since 2011*, about **25,000 hectares** of forests have been *preserved or recovered* through the state’s *Programa Reflorestar*. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))

2. **Breakdown of the 25,000 ha**  
   - Roughly **12,000 hectares** are areas restored from degradation. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  
   - Approximately **13,000 hectares** are existing native vegetation preserved. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))

3. **Supporting Figures**  
   - Around **6,000 rural producer families** have benefited. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  
   - Total investment through *payments for environmental services* (PSA) is ~ **R$ 110 million**. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))

4. **Context & Related Policies**  
   - The state has launched a *Plano Estadual de Recuperação da Vegetação Nativa (PERVN Capixaba)*, which aims to restore **at least 30,000 hectares** by 2030. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/Media/Documentos/PERVN%20final.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
   - Another initiative, *Reflorestar Doce*, is planned for the Rio Doce basin, targeting **~ 6,800 hectares** from 2025–2029 with ~ **R$ 334 million** in investment. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  

5. **Monitoring Results & Deforestation Trends**  
   - According to satellite monitoring (SAD Mata Atlântica from MapBiomas), average annual deforestation in Espírito Santo for **2024–2025** was about **61% lower** than in **2022–2023**. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  
   - Number of deforestation events dropped ~53% in the same comparison. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  
   - Specific figures: 503 hectares deforested in 2022; 363 ha in 2023; 137 ha in 2024; 2025 saw 202 ha. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Primary Source vs Independent Confirmation

- **Primary Source**: The official website of Espírito Santo’s environmental agency (SEAMA) provides detailed data on the Reflorestar program: hectares preserved vs restored, investments, beneficiary families. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))

- **Independent Reporting**: At least one independent outlet, *RedeTV! ES / Folhapress*, reported the same numbers and findings, closely following the SEAMA data. ([esemrede.com.br](https://esemrede.com.br/es-recupera-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-e-reduz-desmatamento-em-61/?utm_source=openai))

---

## Limitations & Clarifications

- The figure of **25,000 hectares** is cumulative *since 2011*, not a recent or single-year result. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  
- The *30,000 hectare* target is a goal under the PERVN for the year **2030**, not yet achieved. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/Media/Documentos/PERVN%20final.pdf?utm_source=openai))  
- The reductions in deforestation are based on recent annual averages and satellite monitoring; these are measured outcomes. ([seama.es.gov.br](https://seama.es.gov.br/espirito-santo-ja-preservou-e-recuperou-25-mil-hectares-de-florestas-por-meio-do-programa-reflorestar?utm_source=openai))  

---

If you like, I can also check for any criticisms, uncertainties, or possible discrepancies in these data.

Here is what I found, with evidence, about the headline *“Successful rare heart valve surgery performed in Vietnam”*:

---

### What the sources actually report

1. **Valves-in-valves surgery in Vietnam**  
   Doctors at the Vietnam National Heart Institute (VNHI) successfully performed a *valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR)* on an **82-year-old male patient** whose prior biological aortic valve had severely degenerated. Because of his health risks, open-heart surgery was deemed unsafe, and the less invasive catheter-based procedure was chosen. After the ~30-minute surgery, his hemodynamics improved, and his condition became stable. ([vietnamnet.vn](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/vn-cardiologists-successfully-perform-valve-in-valve-replacement-for-first-time-2204516.html?utm_source=openai))

   - This operation is noted as **the first valve-in-valve replacement of its kind in Vietnam**. ([vietnamnet.vn](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/vn-cardiologists-successfully-perform-valve-in-valve-replacement-for-first-time-2204516.html?utm_source=openai))

2. **Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) for a 91-year-old patient**  
   Another case reported: a **91-year-old woman from Hà Nội** with severe comorbidities underwent TAVI at E Hospital. After a 90-minute procedure, she was extubated about four hours later. She then rapidly improved: four hours post-procedure she could sit up, eventually walk and feed herself. ([vietnamnews.vn](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1781839/transcatheter-aortic-valve-implantation-opens-lifeline-for-critically-patients.html?utm_source=openai))

3. **Other similar surgeries**  
   - A **Cambodian patient** with a severely calcified bicuspid aortic valve and obesity received TAVI at FV Hospital in Vietnam. The procedure took ~120 minutes and was successful. ([vir.com.vn](https://vir.com.vn/cambodian-patient-treated-for-severe-aortic-stenosis-in-vietnam-165521.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - At Ho Chi Minh City University Medical Center, they marked their **100th successful TAVI** procedure on October 16, 2025. ([vietnamnews.vn](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1727567/university-medical-centre-marks-100th-transcatheter-aortic-valve-implantation.html?utm_source=openai))  
   - First complete endoscopic *Bentall surgery* (which includes replacement of aortic root plus valve and reimplantation of coronary arteries), using small incisions and 3D endoscopic imaging, was successfully done on November 17, 2026 in Ho Chi Minh City. ([vietnam.vn](https://www.vietnam.vn/en/lan-dau-thuc-hien-thanh-cong-phau-thuat-bentall-trong-dieu-tri-tim-mach-phuc-tap?utm_source=openai))

---

### What was *not* found / unsure

- I found **no verified source** exactly matching the phrasing *“a rare heart valve surgery successfully performed in Vietnam”* with the same details as in the candidate headline (i.e. “rare” + “heart valve surgery” + date ~November 2026) beyond those above.

- The given **Vietnam.vn** article hinted in the hint (“Berhasil melakukan operasi penggantian katup aorta yang langka…”) seems not to appear in my searches. There was no verifiable Vietnam.vn article matching that phrase in any language version that I could locate.

- The candidate headline seems to conflate or generalize: multiple sources describe different “rare” or “first-time” or advanced heart valve surgeries, but none exactly match all aspects of the summary provided (especially “rare” + “successful heart valve surgery” without qualification, as of November 21, 2026).

---

### Evaluation: What *actually* happened

- A validated case: A first-of-its-kind **valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve replacement** was done on an 82-year-old male patient in Vietnam. This surgery replaced a degenerated biological aortic valve using catheter-based approach instead of open-heart surgery. Outcome: improved hemodynamics and stabilized condition. ([vietnamnet.vn](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/vn-cardiologists-successfully-perform-valve-in-valve-replacement-for-first-time-2204516.html?utm_source=openai))

- Additional cases (TAVI in very old patients, or with complicating factors such as bicuspid valve, obesity) represent recent, real successes in advanced heart valve procedures. ([vietnamnews.vn](https://vietnamnews.vn/society/1781839/transcatheter-aortic-valve-implantation-opens-lifeline-for-critically-patients.html?utm_source=openai))

---

### Conclusion: What to include in a factual note

- Yes — there *were* successful and in some cases first-of-their-kind heart valve surgeries in Vietnam recently, including advanced catheter-based techniques (TAVI, valve-in-valve replacement).  
- The headline “Successful rare heart valve surgery performed in Vietnam” likely refers to one of these cases, most plausibly the valve-in-valve replacement done by VNHI on an 82-year-old patient, or a TAVI in an elderly or high-risk individual.  
- But based on available evidence as of **November 21, 2026**, there is *no single original report* matching **exactly** the generic claim in the candidate headline. The generic summary is a reasonable description of several events, but not of a distinct, isolated new event beyond those already documented.

---

If you want, I can try to find if the specific Vietnam.vn article referenced actually exists, its date, and its details — to see whether it's just an announcement or something with new information.

Here is what the sources show actually *happened* in the case(s) of domestic worker rescues in Brazil recently, with clear distinction between *launches/plans* versus *completed outcomes*:

---

## Case 1: Embu das Artes, Greater São Paulo — Woman rescued after ~35 years

**What occurred (completed outcome):**

- On **12 November 2026**, a woman (~59 years old) was rescued from a residence in **Embu das Artes** (metropolitan São Paulo) after living for about **35 years** in conditions analogous to slavery, without salary, formal employment recognition, or basic labor rights. ([linproxy.fan.workers.dev](https://linproxy.fan.workers.dev/https/g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2026/11/19/separada-do-filho-ainda-bebe-mulher-e-resgatada-apos-35-anos-trabalhando-sem-salario-em-casa-de-familia-na-grande-sp.ghtml?utm_source=openai))  
- She performed domestic work (cleaning, laundry, cooking, care of animals) and also feirante work (selling goods in public markets), all without compensation. ([linproxy.fan.workers.dev](https://linproxy.fan.workers.dev/https/g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2026/11/19/separada-do-filho-ainda-bebe-mulher-e-resgatada-apos-35-anos-trabalhando-sem-salario-em-casa-de-familia-na-grande-sp.ghtml?utm_source=openai))  
- She was separated from her infant son in the 1990s: the employer did not allow the baby in the house, so he was handed to her brother, and since then she has had no contact. ([metropoles.com](https://www.metropoles.com/sao-paulo/trabalhadora-domestica-e-resgatada-em-sp-apos-35-anos-sem-remuneracao?utm_source=openai))  
- Residences conditions were degrading: she slept in a poorly maintained, isolated room, near dogs, with bad odor; lacked a proper bathroom and had to use a bowl to bathe. ([linproxy.fan.workers.dev](https://linproxy.fan.workers.dev/https/g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2026/11/19/separada-do-filho-ainda-bebe-mulher-e-resgatada-apos-35-anos-trabalhando-sem-salario-em-casa-de-familia-na-grande-sp.ghtml?utm_source=openai))  
- Legal/administrative outcome: the **Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT-SP)** negotiated a *Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC)* on **19 November 2026** with the employing family. They agreed to:
  - Recognize her employment relationship from **1 June 1993** to **12 November 2026** ([metropoles.com](https://www.metropoles.com/sao-paulo/trabalhadora-domestica-e-resgatada-em-sp-apos-35-anos-sem-remuneracao?utm_source=openai))  
  - Pay **≈ R$ 1,736,667.15** in back wages and labor entitlements (salary, overtime, vacations, 13th salary, etc.) ([metropoles.com](https://www.metropoles.com/sao-paulo/trabalhadora-domestica-e-resgatada-em-sp-apos-35-anos-sem-remuneracao?utm_source=openai))  
  - Provide a lifelong pension equivalent to **two minimum wages per month** ([prt2.mpt.mp.br](https://prt2.mpt.mp.br/1391-mpt-firma-acordo-para-garantir-pensao-vitalicia-a-trabalhadora-domestica-resgatada-de-condicoes-analogas-a-escravidao-em-embu-das-artes?utm_source=openai))  

- Post-rescue support: she is being assisted by social services (CREAS), and has the right to six installments of a special unemployment insurance for rescued workers. ([linproxy.fan.workers.dev](https://linproxy.fan.workers.dev/https/g1.globo.com/sp/sao-paulo/noticia/2026/11/19/separada-do-filho-ainda-bebe-mulher-e-resgatada-apos-35-anos-trabalhando-sem-salario-em-casa-de-familia-na-grande-sp.ghtml?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Case 2: 62-year-old woman in Ceará — rescued after 55 years without pay

**What occurred:**

- Earlier in the year, **2 July 2026**, a 62-year-old woman was rescued in **Ceará** (northeastern Brazil) after **55 years** working as an unpaid domestic servant for the same family (three generations), never receiving salary or vacation. ([www1.folha.uol.com.br](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2026/07/domestic-worker-rescued-from-luxury-gated-community-in-brazil-after-55-years-without-pay.shtml?utm_source=openai))  
- Authorities involved: Brazilian Labor Inspectorate, Labor Prosecutor’s Office, Federal Police. ([www1.folha.uol.com.br](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2026/07/domestic-worker-rescued-from-luxury-gated-community-in-brazil-after-55-years-without-pay.shtml?utm_source=openai))  
- Outcome: as of report, she was to be compensated by her employers; estimates of unpaid wages and benefits exceeded **US$ 290,000**. ([www1.folha.uol.com.br](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2026/07/domestic-worker-rescued-from-luxury-gated-community-in-brazil-after-55-years-without-pay.shtml?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Additional Context

- These are not isolated or planned announcements: both are *actual rescues*, with verified governmental inspections, investigations, and legal or administrative agreements.  
- The Embu das Artes rescue is recent (mid-November 2026) and includes a legally binding agreement. The Ceará case occurred earlier in July 2026, with compensation estimates made. ([www1.folha.uol.com.br](https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/brazil/2026/07/domestic-worker-rescued-from-luxury-gated-community-in-brazil-after-55-years-without-pay.shtml?utm_source=openai))  

---

## Clarifications & Gaps

- The original candidate headline (“Rescue of a domestic worker from slavery is significant”) lacked many specifics. It is now clear that this refers most likely to one of the above two cases—commonly cited in Brazilian media: either the Embu das Artes or Ceará case.  
- The source hint “amur.info” did not appear among credible primary sources in searches (government, major press). No evidence was found that *amur.info* is the original source; in fact, Brazilian outlets like G1, UOL, Folha, MPT-SP reported with details.  

---

If you want, I can help track down the “amur.info” version to see whether it adds or repeats details—and whether it may have misreported anything in these cases.
